title: The role templates carry Policy 2's four refusals (DEC-820), DEC-861's record rule and the stop after two refusals (DEC-1137 (2); a template delta through DEC-1116's route)

waits_on.reason: W2-128 still holds template/governance/kernel/templates/** in its paths; it writes no role template again (its text is approved, DEC-1116), but the CTO confirms that before this ticket starts

success.line: Each of the seven role templates (role-cto, role-engineer, role-lead, role-product-spec, role-research, role-reviewer, role-test-designer) states, in one statement, that reads are open and that only four things are refused, in DEC-820 item 2's words: (a) secrets and keys, never printed; (b) the held-out qualification material's contents (its file names may be seen); (c) the counterpart's work on the same ticket; (d) the hidden half of an evaluation set; the statement ends with [DEC-820]
success.verify: tests/acceptance/W2-175/: for each of the seven files, one statement (a paragraph, a list item or a table row, whitespace collapsed) carries `read` with `open`, `secret`, `held-out`, `counterpart` and `hidden half` and ends with `[DEC-820]`; red on the base (no template cites DEC-820 for it)

success.line: The counterpart refusal (c) is stated in each role's own half: role-engineer says the engineer never reads this ticket's acceptance-test code and may run its cases and see names, pass or fail and failure messages; role-test-designer says the designer never reads this ticket's implementation (the branch's changes other than its own tests) and works from the specification, the KPI lines and the existing code; role-reviewer says a reviewer reads everything, tests and code alike [DEC-820 item 2 (c) and item 3, DEC-957, DEC-963]
success.verify: tests/acceptance/W2-175/: three string tests, one per file, each on one statement carrying a negation (`never`, `not`) for the engineer's and the designer's, and `everything` with `tests` and `code` for the reviewer's; and tests/acceptance/W2-128/test_w2_128_templates.py::test_s3_engineer_template_holds_no_instruction_to_read_the_acceptance_tests still passes

success.line: Each of the six templates role-engineer, role-test-designer, role-product-spec, role-research, role-reviewer and role-lead states that the owner's decisions are recorded by the orchestrator's decision-record commits and that no worker or lead puts `Role: owner` or `Decided-by:` on a commit; role-cto keeps its decision-record commit line (`Task: decision-record`, `Role: orchestrator`, `Decided-by: owner (chat, {DATE})`) unchanged [DEC-861]
success.verify: tests/acceptance/W2-175/: for each of the six, one statement carries `decision-record`, `owner` and `Role: owner`, and ends with `[DEC-861]`; for role-cto, the line of the base is still there byte for byte (a test reads it from `git show` of the base commit)

success.line: Each of the seven role templates carries, word for word, the stop sentence of the brief envelope's return section: "Refused twice for the same call: stop and say so. Never work around a refusal: report it." [DEC-1137 (2)]
success.verify: tests/acceptance/W2-175/: each of the seven files holds that sentence, and the sentence is a substring of brief.md too (one source of wording, so TPL-6 F1's conflict cannot arise)

success.line: Each changed role template's `version` goes from 1.0.0 to 1.0.1 (DEC-1121's step for a template delta); no other front matter key changes, and the prose of each stays within its budget in `governance/project/facts.yaml` (3500 characters, role-lead 8000, role-cto 6000) with every placeholder a key of `keys.yaml` [DEC-1050, DEC-1116, DEC-1121]
success.verify: tests/acceptance/W2-175/: the front matter of each changed file parses with `version: 1.0.1` and the other keys equal the base's; tests/acceptance/W2-128/test_w2_128_templates.py::test_s2_prose_is_within_r3_budget and ::test_s5_every_key_placeholder_is_in_keys_yaml pass for all seven

success.line: The cases of W2-128, W2-152 and W2-153 that read the role templates still pass with the new text (the gov brief golden files, the template tests, the launch delivery) [DEC-1050, DEC-1116]
success.verify: `PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/src python3 -m pytest tests/acceptance/W2-128 tests/acceptance/W2-152 tests/acceptance/W2-153 -q -p no:cacheprovider` exits 0 in the ticket's worktree, run through the heavy-job gate

success.line: The change goes through DEC-1116's route, recorded in docs/changes/W2-175-CIT-P.md: the template delta (each changed file, its base and new sha256, the lines added), the independent review's READY, and the owner's approval of the new bytes; the record's `status` is ACCEPTED only after that approval, and the kernel set is promoted at the approved bytes [CAP-33, DEC-1116, DEC-1137 (2)]
success.verify: docs/changes/W2-175-CIT-P.md has a section per CAP-33 step (evidence, proposal, independent review, owner's approval, versioned promotion); the sha256 column equals `sha256sum` of each file at the ticket's head; the file's `decisions_read` and `decisions_carried` cite DEC-1137, DEC-820 and DEC-861

failure.line: A role template line that states a rule cites a PROPOSED or superseded decision for it, or states a stop rule that differs from brief.md's [DEC-1073, TPL-6 F1]
failure.verify: tests/acceptance/W2-128/test_w2_128_templates.py::test_f7_every_bracketed_decision_id_in_a_template_is_accepted passes for the seven files; the substring test of the stop sentence (success line 4) fails when one file's sentence is changed by a letter

failure.line: The ticket's diff names any file beyond the seven role templates and docs/changes/W2-175-CIT-P.md: not brief.md, a `brief-*.md` pointer, keys.yaml, facts.yaml, a skill, a file under `roles/`, any `.claude/` or `.rulesync/` path [DEC-1137, DEC-315]
failure.verify: `git diff --name-only <base>..HEAD` of the ticket's branch lists only those paths (a close-time check; the guard refuses the rest at write time)

non_goals: no change to brief.md, the five `brief-*.md` pointers (they stay as W2-128 left them, DEC-1137 (1)), keys.yaml, facts.yaml or the role files under roles/
no change to the orchestration skill or any skill (W2-11 holds them)
the `.claude/templates/role-*.md` copies are not written here: the copies ACT writes them after the owner's approval (DEC-315)
no new rule beyond the three the owner named (DEC-1137 (2)); no rewording of the rules the templates already carry
